verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly's own docs cover member role assignment: base roles, preset roles, and custom roles you create, with directly assigned roles overriding the base role. Separately, API access tokens can be scoped to restrict which operations they can perform, such as read-only integrations. Together these deliver the core of restricting who can change flags. The evidence does not show how finely custom-role policies can target specific flags or environments. missing for 10: explicit evidence of per-flag/per-environment resource scoping in role policies, detail on the permission policy model, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can restrict who can change which flags with roles, permissions, and scoped API tokens

citations.quote: If a member is directly assigned a role, such as a preset role or a role that you create, that role is used instead of the member's base role
You assign roles directly to members when you invite them to LaunchDarkly.
You can scope your API tokens to restrict the set of operations they can perform. For example, you can build an integration that only has read access
